figs.title: Polleve-4: find each COOH, step to the α carbon, look for an OH there
figs.caption: The five structures of DPAW slide 45, drawn from the Atlas. Marked on each: the COOH, the carbon next to its carbon (α), and an OH on an α carbon (or on the β carbon). The line under each is worked out from the same marked atoms: three are alpha-hydroxy acids. Rule: slide 44, "OH on alpha-C (i.e., carbon next to -CO2H)"; "Hydroxy group needs to be ... on the carbon that is next to the carboxylic acid" (T@23455–23600).

figs.title: Glycolic acid: the OH sits on the α carbon, the carbon next to the COOH
figs.caption: Glycolic acid, HO-CH2-COOH, from the Atlas (DPAW slide 43). The hydroxy acid SAR of slide 44: a COOH group, and the OH on the alpha carbon, the carbon next to CO2H.

figs.title: Salicylic acid: count from the COOH carbon, α then β; the OH is on β
figs.caption: Salicylic acid from the Atlas (DPAW slide 43). The ring carbon next to the COOH carbon is alpha and carries no OH; the OH is on the next carbon, beta, two carbons from the COOH carbon (T@22090–22230).

figs.title: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid has its OH on C2, the α carbon; 2-hydroxybenzoic acid on the β carbon
figs.caption: Lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid, DPAW slide 68) and salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid, slide 43) from the Atlas, marked by the slide 44 test: an OH on the alpha carbon, the carbon next to CO2H. The other two options are not drawn.

figs.title: The hydroxy acid SAR: COOH, OH on the α carbon, and R (mostly alkyl) on that carbon
figs.caption: The slide 44 SAR drawn on its own example (R = CH3, lactic acid), from the Atlas: R is the group on the alpha carbon, "mostly archal [alkyl] groups" (T@22839–23200).

figs.title: Rings A, B and C are six-membered; ring D (C13–C17) is five-membered
figs.caption: Hydrocortisone from the Atlas, numbered as on DPAW slide 20. Ring D, the five-membered ring, carries the side chain at C17.

figs.title: C10: the A/B junction carbon that carries the methyl C19
figs.caption: The numbering skeleton of DPAW slide 20, from the Atlas: C1 to C10 around rings A and B, C11 to C17 through rings C and D, C18 on C13, C19 on C10, the side chain from C20 on C17 (T 1003–1016, 1084–1092).

figs.title: C11: in ring C, next to ring B
figs.caption: The numbering skeleton of DPAW slide 20, from the Atlas. "If you know where your 1 is, you know where your 11 is, and your 17" (T 1098–1099).

figs.title: C17: the side chain starts with C20 on C17
figs.caption: The numbering skeleton of DPAW slide 20, from the Atlas. C17 is the last ring carbon in ring D; the side chain begins with C20 (T 1015–1016, 1088–1090).

figs.title: The angular methyls: C18 on C13, C19 on C10
figs.caption: The numbering skeleton of DPAW slide 20, from the Atlas. After C17 the two angular methyls are numbered: C18 on C13 first, then C19 on C10 (T 1012–1014, 1088–1089).

figs.title: The four SAR features on one glucocorticoid
figs.caption: Fluticasone propionate, the Atlas's example of the four features of DPAW slide 20 (drawn on slide 24): C1–C2 double bond, 6α-halogen, 9α-halogen, 11β-OH (T 1019–1075). α bonds are hashed (away from you), β bonds wedged (toward you).

figs.title: The halogens are α (hashed), the C11 hydroxyl is β (wedged)
figs.caption: Fluticasone propionate from the Atlas (DPAW slides 20, 24): 6α-X and 9α-X point away from you, the 11β-OH toward you (T 1067–1072).

figs.title: The 9α-halogen of the slide 24 derivatives is fluorine
figs.caption: Fluticasone propionate from the Atlas (DPAW slide 24), one of the derivatives with a 9α-fluorine.

figs.title: The added C1–C2 double bond: hydrocortisone beside clobetasol propionate
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas, as compared on DPAW slide 25: ring A of hydrocortisone has a single bond between C1 and C2; clobetasol propionate has the double bond (T 1175–1179).

figs.title: Hydrocortisone to clobetasol propionate: groups added and a C1–C2 double bond
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas, as compared on DPAW slide 25. Marked on clobetasol propionate are the changes he pointed to on hydrocortisone, "not metabolism" (T 1140–1145, 1175–1179).

figs.title: The groups that hydrogen-bond in the receptor, and one that cannot
figs.caption: Hydrocortisone from the Atlas; the hydrogen bonds of DPAW slide 23: C3 carbonyl (two), 11β-OH, C20 carbonyl, C21-OH, 17α-OH (T 1131–1139). The C18 methyl has no hydrogen-bond donor or acceptor.

figs.title: Six hydrogen bonds, from five groups
figs.caption: Hydrocortisone from the Atlas, with the receptor residues of DPAW slide 23 (T 1131–1139). The C3 carbonyl makes two of the six.

figs.title: 11β: the β-oriented OH on carbon 11
figs.caption: Hydrocortisone from the Atlas (DPAW slide 26), numbered as on slide 20: 11β-HSD acts at C11, where hydrocortisone carries its 11β-OH (wedged: toward the viewer).

figs.title: Hydrocortisone's 11β-OH, cortisone's C11 ketone
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas, as drawn on DPAW slide 26: 11β-HSD oxidizes the 11β-OH of hydrocortisone to the 11-ketone of cortisone. The 11β-OH is one of the SAR features of slide 20.

figs.title: UV light opens the B ring of 7-dehydrocholesterol
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas (DPAW slide 27). The atoms of ring B are marked in both; in cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) the ring is open (Vitamin D reading (Endotext), lines 60–62).

figs.title: A secosteroid: a steroid with one ring opened
figs.caption: From the Atlas (DPAW slide 27): ring B, closed in 7-dehydrocholesterol, is open in calcipotriene, as in cholecalciferol (T@2989–3200).

figs.title: Pimecrolimus and tacrolimus: Cl vs OH, ethyl vs allyl
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas (DPAW slide 28, where the two differences are highlighted): pimecrolimus carries Cl and an ethyl group, tacrolimus OH and an allyl group (T@4600–4780). The macrolide skeletons otherwise match.

figs.title: The circled group: an ester inside the ring, a lactone
figs.caption: Pimecrolimus from the Atlas (DPAW slide 32, Polleve-3). The -C(=O)-O- link is part of the large ring: a cyclic ester, a lactone (slide 28: "Macrolide or lactone immunosuppressants").

figs.title: A ring closed through an ester (lactone) or through amides (lactam)
figs.caption: Pimecrolimus (DPAW slides 28, 32) and cyclosporine (slide 33), from the Atlas. Each amide bond of cyclosporine's ring is marked.

figs.title: Cyclosporine: amide bonds closed into a ring, a cyclic amide (lactam)
figs.caption: Cyclosporine from the Atlas (DPAW slide 33): eleven amino acids joined by amide (peptide) bonds, every one marked, closed into a ring (T@12100–12254).

figs.title: Methotrexate and folic acid: N-CH₃ for N-H, NH₂ for OH
figs.caption: Both from the Atlas, side by side as on DPAW slide 31: the same pteridine, p-aminobenzoic acid and glutamic acid parts; the two points of difference are marked (T@8700–8800).

figs.caption: Methotrexate from the Atlas, marked with the SAR of DPAW slide 31 (T@10096–10900).
